He refused to be flexible with me despite me demonstrating several times that I really needed his help. I felt defeated and like I had no one else to turn to. Oh and the TA's sucked!!

Course structure:
3 Exams - (25% each)
7 MindTap (Cengage) Problem Sets - (5% each) ---> 2 lowest ones get dropped

All in all, I strongly encourage you to take this class with another professor whether that is here at UMD or at a community college. The negatives far outweigh the positives unfortunately...

Lectures are SO boring but still giving him 5 stars. Exams are pretty fair, did find the past exams to usually be easier than the real exams (mcqs mostly), but with the curve it didn't really matter (final grade curve was VERY generous). Although the lectures could be dull, you could tell he is a super smart dude and explains everything really well. He posts slides and lecture videos so if you have a hard time focusing in class, which I did, I find sometimes it can be best to just take the notes from the slideshow and refer to the lecture video when you are confused and need a more in depth explanation (examples especially). For exams, there are double sided full page formula sheets that you can also add your own stuff to, these were super helpful, and for the final it's two pages front and back. He is also a very sweet guy, he'll make jokes every once in a while and is very nice if you ever go talk to him or ask him any questions. Homework is 15% of your grade and graded solely on completion, which is a great grade boost and the problem set questions are very relevant to exams. There are problem sets once a week and no reading so most of the work for this class is just studying well. 

Overall really liked this class with Shea I learned a lot!
Honeslty I took this class during the winter and best decision. its all online and ur own paste. The assignments are not bad at all, and the exams are like the practice ones. I strongly recommend
The whole class is asynchronous and on your own pace. There are three problem sets, a midterm exam, and a final exam.
I had him fall semester and he’s an easy class for 201. Doesn’t assign much work and his exams are easy. All you have to do is review the slides the night before and you’ll do fine on the exams.

Took this in the fall and the reviews are extremely misleading for professor Sarna...besides the fact that he can kind of go on tangents sometimes. This class isn't really that bad if you've taken an econ class before, but if you haven't it can definitely be a mindset adjustment for sure. If you do the chapter readings, take notes, use chat to check over your problem sets and study a minimal amount before the exam you will be fine. Use the lectures as a discussion of the chapter readings you've done, so you should try and stay on top of you readings (most important and challenging part of the class IMO). Also the average for the class was like really low which means Sarna basically had a 12% curve every exam, so I got an 100 on every exam except the first one from the curve alone. Sarna himself isn't the easiest lecturer to follow, but again, doing the readings makes him 100 times easier to understand. Essentially if you do what you need to you will do great in the class.

I think this is genuinely one of the worst classes I have ever taken. The professor is very knowledgeable in his subject but that does not mean he is a good professor. This was simply a horrific class, unless you understand analogies and metaphors on a topic you have no prior knowledge in this is the class for you. His lectures are very slow and hard to comprehend, when he isn't reading off the slides, he is providing a long winded story that is gives to try to explain the topic and just makes it harder to understand. This class will be you doing all the work yourself, I have had to rely entirely on the textbook because whenever I went to lecture I just ended up more confused. If you already understand macro then this would be the class for you, if you really wanna learn then do not take this course with him. He was constantly unwilling to work with students and it seems like he genuinely hates his job. This class will destroy your gpa.

I'm not sure why his ratings are so low. His exams are actually pretty manageable—they’re all multiple choice, and there are only three total exams (two midterms and a final). The only other assignments are seven problem sets, and he drops the lowest two, which helps if you have a busy week or don’t do as well on one. He also does exam reviews and even dedicates a class to going over a mock exam, which is really helpful for understanding what to expect. Another plus is that he uploads the lecture slides after class, and they’re very useful for studying and reviewing the material. The only downside is that the lectures themselves aren’t the most engaging, but the slides and reviews make it pretty straightforward to do well if you stay on top of the work.

On the second exam, the class average was a failing grade. This was a direct result of the professor failing to provide study material relevant to the questions on the exam. There was no curve, after 4/400 students got a grade in the 90s. Luckily, the lowest exam grade is dropped, but this result is still inexcusable - take another professor if possible.

name: ECON201
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: Prerequisite: MATH107 or MATH110; or must have math eligibility of MATH113 or higher. Recommended: ECON200. Credit only granted for: ECON201 or ECON205. An introduction to how market economies behave at the aggregate level. The determination of national income/output and the problems of unemployment inflation, will be examined, along with monetary and fiscal policy.
